narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: Cultural historian or traditional dance practitioner.
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Living Totem: Asia's Peacock Dances
This is Peacock dance. Traditional/20th Century.
on_screen: Title card: Peacock dance · China, India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh · Traditional/20th Century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance has deep roots in Asian folk traditions, with specific regional evolutions.
The Dai peacock dance is tied to ancient ethnic culture and totemism.
The Indonesian Tari Merak is a 20th-century creation by Raden Tjeje Soemantri.
on_screen: Map: China, India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh · Global

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is used for festivals (Water Festival, Thai Pongal), spiritual rituals, and welcoming guests.
It expresses joy and honors cultural totems.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Peacock dance, at Botanical Garden Hyderabad.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4a/Peacock_dance%2C_at_Botanical_Garden_Hyderabad.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dai dancers use either a heavy bamboo-and-silk frame or perform 'unarmed' without props.
Tari Merak dancers use classical Sundanese movements to mimic the bird.
Mayilattam performers dress as peacocks for harvest festivals.
Watch for Feather stretching.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears

The Dai peacock dance music is driven by the rhythmic interplay of elephant-foot drums, gongs, and cymbals.

Mayilattam dancers dress as peacocks.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Raden Tjeje Soemantri (choreographer of the Indonesian Tari Merak).
Dai (China), Mayilattam (India), Tari Merak (Indonesia), and traditions in Myanmar, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh.
The dance is a folk tradition in most regions, with the Indonesian variant being a 20th-century classical-folk hybrid.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Peacock dance is variant of Mayilattam: The Indian peacock dance tradition.
Peacock dance is variant of Tari Merak: The Indonesian peafowl dance.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: The Dai peacock dance is a spiritual totem and essential to cultural festivals; the Mayilattam is performed in honor of Lord Murugan. Outsiders should observe local customs regarding festival participation.

scenes.title: Until next time
narration: Explore how the movements of the peacock have inspired centuries of ritual and performance across Asia.

music_brief.purpose: original soundtrack faithful to the tradition, with documented commercial reuse rights and no recurring royalties
music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.sound_description: The Dai peacock dance music is driven by the rhythmic interplay of elephant-foot drums, gongs, and cymbals.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Peacock dance (China, India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh). Instruments: Elephant-foot drums, Gongs, Cymbals. Mood: Joyful, Celebratory. It should sound like this: The Dai peacock dance music is driven by the rhythmic interplay of elephant-foot drums, gongs, and cymbals. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.

wardrobe.policy: neutral dress with a respectful nod (palette and fabric only): the sources describe sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire, or the dance is sacred
